questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good University, close to city, country I wanted to visit

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. The university had a website that was easy to navigate.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The RAs helped me find my university accommodation and answered questions I had about the area – closest supermarket, bus routes, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorm rooms at varying price levels (though all quite expensive), depending on the level of luxury.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Unfurnished kitchen with a microwave, toaster and kettle, but without an oven – which I shared with five others. Apart from that, there were places on campus where you could buy food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It is a good way to meet other students – both exchange students and other students – and by living on campus, you are sure to be close to any events that might take place on campus.

Make sure to have a cleaning schedule with those you live with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of dorm rooms, but they were very expensive, as there is currently a cost of living crisis in Dublin.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite intuitive – there was a form on the university website, and it was easy to find the information I needed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I suppose I could have emailed the person responsible for exchange students at the university – they seemed happy to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite, although some classes were on one form/website and others were on another, which in some cases made me take other classes than I'd originally planned so that I just had to use one form. But I was satisfied with the classes I ended up taking.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most of the classes are worth few ECTS, which allows you to take classes that are a bit outside your field. My advice would be to take a class that teaches you something about the country/city of your university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were ranked from 1-5 depending on level, and as a BA student I was allowed to take level 1-3 courses as far as I remember. A number of the courses were recommended especially for exchange students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH my classes are usually longer, and you are urged to actively participate and be part of the discussion. At UCD most of my classes were one hour twice a week, and they were lectures with little to no active student participation. Some of my classes were more in the style of those I have at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AH20280	Queer Art Histories
ENG10020 Children's Literature
ENG20440 Reading the story of Ireland: Irish Literature in English
ENG32510 Writing Dublin
HIS20780 History of Science
IR10050 Irish for Beginners/Gaeilge do Thosaitheoirí

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed all my classes. The Irish for Beginners gaelic language course taught me a bit about Irish history and culture and I would recommend that to students from all fields.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think there was anything unexpected, except price levels

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The price of accommodation was a surprise, but it would have been difficult to find accommodation myself, and probably also expensive so I am still glad I chose university housing.

Public transport was quite cheap when I was in Dublin – 1 euro for up to 1,5 hours of transport for students/young adults.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs at the university, and it was easy to find information on them. I would definitely recommend joining a club, as there are so many of them that it is unlikely for there not to be one that would interest you, and it is a good way to meet people.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: sports, religious, language, field specific, literature and movies, politics, food, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Choosing a club is about personal preference, but I'd definitely recommend looking into them. I like the movie club, as it allowed you to meet people and watch movies in the campus cinema at a very low cost – I think just 2 euro for the whole semester, which was the price level for most clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to other cities in Ireland – Belfast, Galway of Cork for example – to see other places in Ireland. There is also a coastline train track that leads you to coastal towns close to Dublin where you can go hiking or just visit a beautiful place outside the city. Also, I would recommend visiting some of the beautiful, old pubs in Dublin.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite – it is not so different from Denmark. I liked Dublin, as it was easy to navigate and very charming. People were more talkative than in Denmark, but that was quite nice!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mainly socialised with other exchange students, but join a club or talk to someone in class would bemy advice for socialising with any student at the university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food options are more so processed or unhealthy food than in Denmark, if you want to buy something on the go or something pre-cooked that you just need to heat up at home. Also, organic produce is not as common, but can usually be found on a shelf in the supermarket.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The music, literature, friendliness to strangers, and the pub culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure to find accommodation a little while before you leave. It is not easy to find, and a good idea would maybe be to find university housing or to rent near the university.
2. Join some clubs or attend social events – a large part of the exchange experience is meeting new people!
3. Try to see some of the other parts of Ireland as well! It is a beautiful country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a different country, the friendships and taking interesting classes that are not available at my home university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: When I had just arrived and was the only person at my accommodation and did not know anyone, or where anything was. It got a lot easier when the others arrived and we could figure things out together.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
